item.title: Comings and Goings
item.description: This new Mexican restaurant is a love letter to Baja Mexico that has landed in the Design District mailbox, with us as the lucky recipients.

item.title: Jesuit Starting Strong in Playoffs
item.description: The round robin portion of the AT&T Metroplex High School Hockey League playoffs is underway and Jesuit Dallas is off to a hot start, picking up a pair of wins this week.

item.title: Dallas Goethe Institut to Host German Author
item.description: Open to the public, the event featuring the award-winning author will take place on Feb. 21 at 4 p.m. at Christ Lutheran Church, 3001 Lovers Lane.

item.title: ‘Park Cities People’ Applauds
item.description: Julie Owen Meyer, a former pediatric oncology nurse who has written a classic Jesse Tree Advent book, Our Long-Expected Gift.

item.title: Camera Rolling!
item.description: Highland Park Middle School students are making headlines both behind and in front of the camera thanks to their weekly schoolwide broadcasts on Raider Media News.

item.title: New Dallas Diner Turns Up the Volume
item.description: AM/FM, a new all-day diner in the Design District, quietly opened February 10, but there’s nothing timid about its food, drinks, and vibe. AM/FM just blasted what a stereotypical Texas diner is supposed to be, and it’s going to rock.

item.title: LunarFest to Spread Joy of Spring Festivals
item.description: The community can experience the joy and prosperity of the new lunar year from 2 to 4 p.m. on Feb. 21 during LunarFest at the Moody Family YMCA.

item.title: Lady Scots Open Basketball Playoffs Monday
item.description: Highland Park’s girls basketball team kicks off the Class 5A Division I playoffs Monday when they square off against Frisco Heritage at 7 p.m. in Allen.

item.title: Twice is Nice: ESD Girls Go Back-To-Back
item.description: Episcopal School of Dallas won its first-ever SPC girls basketball crown a year ago.

item.title: Eagles Make it an ESD Sweep at State
item.description: Less than three hours later, and on the same floor the Episcopal School of Dallas girls basketball team became repeat state champions, ESD’s boys made it a sweep by capturing their first SPC title since 2010.
